title: Working Is Not Secure
description: A cipher that encrypts and decrypts correctly can still fail its security claim. Separate correctness, performance and security, and test each one on its own terms.

stops.label: Working Is Not Secure: four questions
stops.note: Start here: correctness, performance and the security claim are three different questions, and a working cipher can still fail the last one.

stops.label: Monoalphabetic Substitution
stops.note: 26! possible keys, yet language patterns survive encryption. The key space bounds only exhaustive search.

stops.label: One-Time Pad
stops.note: Perfect secrecy holds only for a secret, uniform key as long as the message and used once, and secrecy is not authentication.

stops.label: Enigma
stops.note: A working machine with an enormous key space, attacked through changing systems, keys and procedures.

stops.label: Entropy
stops.note: How distributions, independence and key generation decide whether a key space is as large as it looks.

stops.label: Security reductions
stops.note: What “provably as hard as factoring” claims, and what it quietly assumes.

stops.label: Modern Attack Evidence
stops.note: Judge a security test by the access, data, computation and validation behind it.

stops.label: Back to the verdict
stops.note: Correct, fast enough to do by hand, and still insecure: the security claim failed without any key search.
